dod_intent_evidence: DARPA-derived tech, AF SBIR Phase II 2022 ($749,819), Army xTech SBIR Phase II 2025, and a $4.25M USSOCOM S&T Directorate contract announced 2026-05-18 — homepage, SBIR/STTR section, News section.
score_evidence: 'The dismounted warfighter...Using a LightCell...could reduce their load by 75%' → operator_absence (very low/good — operator-centric)
'One LightCell unit weighs less than 10 lbs' and 'requiring 200-300 W of electricity in a man-portable form factor' → deployment_awareness_absence (low/good — genuine SWaP-C fluency)
Open roles include 'Forward Deployed Engineer at a Defense-Tech Startup' → hiring_profile_skew (low/good)
Zero mention of CMMC/NIST 800-171/ITAR/ATO anywhere despite DARPA, AFWERX, and USSOCOM contract volume → deployment_awareness_absence penalty
Simultaneous AF (2022) and Army (2025, 18-month) Phase II SBIRs plus a new $4.25M USSOCOM contract on a ~27-person team → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: Zero mention of CMMC, NIST 800-171, or ITAR anywhere on the site despite DARPA origin, two SBIR Phase IIs, and a $4.25M USSOCOM S&T contract.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A hardware power-generation company handling DoD-funded tactical energy tech at this volume needs company-level CMMC certification before follow-on contracts flow, and thermophotovoltaic power tech for c-UAS/UAS integration is a plausible ITAR item — silence here is the same blind spot that stalls a Phase II-to-Phase III transition.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Founders are MIT engineering researchers focused on the physics/hardware, not government compliance posture.

blind_spots.blind_spot: SBIR abstract describes LightCell 'recharging batteries...in autonomous drone charging stations, in remote unattended ground sensors' — implying networked, remotely monitored charging infrastructure — with no mention of how telemetry/status data gets an ATO to touch GFE networks.
blind_spots.operator_reality: The moment a power unit reports status back to a command network, it needs RMF/ATO just like any other government-network-connected device; a purely hardware-framed pitch skips this step entirely.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team's own language frames the product as pure hardware/energy, not as a networked system, so the software/compliance tail is invisible to them.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: in autonomous drone charging stations, in remote unattended ground sensors, and more

blind_spots.blind_spot: Claims 'military-grade' power generation and compatibility with 'Starlink systems, computers, cell phones' without citing MIL-STD-810 (environmental) or MIL-STD-461 (EMI/EMC) qualification anywhere.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A prime or program office won't accept a power unit into a fielded system of record without documented environmental/EMI qualification — 'military-grade' as marketing language, not a cited test standard, is exactly the gap that stalls GFE integration.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product is still SBIR-stage (TRL 6 target per their own abstract); formal qualification testing likely hasn't happened yet.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Mesodyne would expect to be at TRL 6 by the end of the Phase II effort with this particular application

opener_hook: Mesodyne's $4.25M USSOCOM S&T contract and Army xTech Phase II SBIR are both public — neither the site nor the abstracts mention CMMC or ITAR despite the DARPA lineage.
what_they_do: Builds LightCell, a patented MIT-derived thermophotovoltaic power generator for dismounted warfighters, UAS, and remote sensors, funded through DARPA-origin research plus AF and Army SBIRs and a USSOCOM S&T contract.
